sections.heading: 2.6 Geometrical Interpretation in the Complex Plane
sections.text: In this section, we study the geometrical interpretation of a complex number z in the complex plane and the locus of z in Cartesian form.

sections.heading: Definition 2.5 (Circle in the Complex Plane)
sections.text: A circle is defined as the locus of a point which moves in a plane such that its distance from a fixed point in that plane is always a constant. The fixed point is the centre (z₀) and the constant distance is the radius (r) of the circle.
sections.formula: |z - z₀| = r  (Complex Form of Circle Equation)

sections.heading: Converting Complex Equations to Cartesian Form
sections.text: To find the Cartesian equation of a locus, substitute z = x + iy (where x, y ∈ ℝ), group real and imaginary parts, and evaluate using the modulus definition.

items.label: Example 2.18
items.title: Isosceles Right Triangle in the Argand Plane
items.problem: Given z = 3 + 2i, represent z, iz, and z + iz in one Argand plane and show they form an isosceles right triangle.
steps: Since AB² = BC² = 13 (AB = BC) and AB² + BC² = 13 + 13 = 26 = CA², △ABC is an isosceles right triangle. Q.E.D.

items.label: Example 2.19
items.title: Standardizing Circle Equation
items.problem: Show that |3z - 5 + i| = 4 represents a circle, and find its centre and radius.
steps: This is of the standard form |z - z₀| = r.

items.label: Example 2.20
items.title: Interior Region of Circle
items.problem: Show that |z + 2 - i| < 2 represents interior points of a circle, and find its centre and radius.
steps: This is of the form |z - z₀| < r.
It represents the interior points of a circle with centre z₀ = -2 + i and radius r = 2.

items.label: Example 2.21
items.title: Cartesian Form of Locus
items.problem: Obtain the Cartesian locus of (i) |z| = |z - i|, (ii) |2z - 3 - i| = 3.
steps: (i) Substitute z = x + iy: |x + iy| = |x + i(y - 1)| => x² + y² = x² + (y - 1)² => x² + y² = x² + y² - 2y + 1 => 2y - 1 = 0.

items.label: Question 1
items.problem: If z = x + iy and |(z - 4i)/(z + 4i)| = 1, show that the locus of z is the real axis.
steps: Substitute z = x + iy: |x + i(y - 4)| = |x + i(y + 4)|.
Squaring: x² + (y - 4)² = x² + (y + 4)² => x² + y² - 8y + 16 = x² + y² + 8y + 16.
Since y = 0 represents the x-axis, the locus of z is the real axis. Q.E.D.

items.label: Question 2
items.problem: If z = x + iy and Im((2z + 1)/(iz + 1)) = 0, show that the locus of z is 2x² + 2y² + x - 2y = 0.
steps: Denominator: i(x + iy) + 1 = ix - y + 1 = (1 - y) + ix.
Rationalize: [(2x + 1) + i(2y)][(1 - y) - ix] / [(1 - y)² + x²].
Extract Imaginary Part: [2y(1 - y) - x(2x + 1)] / [(1 - y)² + x²] = 0.

items.label: Question 3
items.problem: Obtain the Cartesian equation for the locus of z = x + iy in: (i) Re(iz²), (ii) Im((1-i)z + 1) = 0, (iii) |z + i| = |z - 1|, (iv) z̄ = z⁻¹.
steps: (i) iz² = i(x + iy)² = i(x² - y² + 2ixy) = -2xy + i(x² - y²). Re(iz²) = -2xy. (Or if iz + 3: -y + 3 = 0).
(iv) z̄ = 1/z => z · z̄ = 1 => |z|² = 1 => x² + y² = 1 (unit circle).

items.label: Question 4
items.problem: Show that the equations represent circles and find center and radius: (i) |z - 2 - i| = 3, (ii) |2z + 2 - 4i| = 2, (iii) |3z - 6 + 12i| = 8.

items.label: Question 5
items.problem: Obtain the Cartesian equation for the locus of z: (i) |z - 4| = 16, (ii) |z - 4|² - |z - 1|² = 16.
